newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-CANTERBURY BEATS WAIKATO WITH 14 MEN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-CANTERBURY BEATS WAIKATO WITH 14 MEN.

text.p: The Canterbury Crusaders, down 10-6 at halftime and then playing with just 14 players, overcame the Waikato Chiefs 24-15 in a fiercely contested Super 12 match on Saturday.
Auckland referee Glen Wahlstrom sent off Canterbury hooker Mark Hammett for punching opponent Greg Smith 13 minutes into the second half of the floodlit match.
Though Hammett was replaced at hooker, the Crusaders had to lose one player and lock Mark Weedon was pulled off by coach Wayne Smith.
Despite the under-strength pack, Canterbury hit back hard with winger Daryl Gibson and prop Kevin Nepia scoring tries.
Paul Mitchell, a Waikato substitute, scored a try to close the gap to 21-15 but Andrew Mehrtens, who had kicked 11 points earlier, shot in a dropped goal to stretch the Crusaders lead to 24-15.
The Chiefs shocked the home side with a stunning try by half-back Rhys Duggan in the first minute of play.

Crusaders full-back Leon MacDonald took a high ball from Ian Foster and tried to set up play. But it appeared that his front rowers were too slow to provide him support and the ball popped out on the Chiefs side. Duggan picked up the ball and scooted to the left corner for a fine try. Matthew Cooper added the conversion.
Cooper missed two penalties before Mehrtens closed the gap with a penalty for the Crusaders, then whittled down the margin with a further penalty in the 32nd minute after missing one.
However, Cooper had the final say before halftime, lifting a fine shot at goal to give his team a 10-6 lead.

Canterbury - Leon MacDonald, Daryl Gibson, Tabai Matson, Mark Mayerhofler, Paula Bale, Andrew Mehrtens, Justin Marshall, Clark McLeod, Angus Gardiner, Todd Blackadder, Mark Weedon, Norman Maxwell, Con Barrell, Mark Hammett, Kevin Nepia.

Waikato - Matthew Cooper, Eric Rush, Frank Bunce, Dion Mathews, Eric Rush, Walter Little, Ian Foster, Rhys Duggan, Errol Brain, Dean Anglesey, Ian Jones, Glenn Taylor, Michael Collins, Greg Smith, Lee Ligard.
